pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing: Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make a story more interesting in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
2. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING
This lesson teaches Guided Writing: Creative Writing for Grade 8 ARABIC.

STUDY STEPS
1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Guided Writing: Creative Writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Guided Writing: Creative Writing above.
2. Explain Guided Writing: Creative Writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Guided Writing: Creative Writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Guided Writing: Creative Writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Guided Writing: Creative Writing important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make a story more interesting in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary
2. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
